claim: Tribolium castaneum has nine type II neuroblast lineages per hemisphere in the embryo.
source_text: Intriguingly, we found nine lineages per hemisphere in the Tribolium embryo while Drosophila produces only eight per brain hemisphere.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations and counting of Tc-pnt-expressing type II neuroblast clusters in Tribolium embryos as described in the Results section.

claim: Drosophila produces eight type II neuroblast lineages per brain hemisphere in the embryo.
source_text: Intriguingly, we found nine lineages per hemisphere in the Tribolium embryo while Drosophila produces only eight per brain hemisphere.
evidence_reasoning: This claim references established knowledge from prior research on Drosophila, as cited in the manuscript (Walsh and Doe, 2017; Álvarez and Díaz-Benjumea, 2018).

claim: Embryonic type II neuroblast lineages are significantly larger in Tribolium than in Drosophila.
source_text: These embryonic lineages are significantly larger in Tribolium than they are in Drosophila and contain more intermediate progenitors.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements and statistical comparisons of lineage sizes between the two species presented in the Results section and Figure 9.

claim: Tribolium embryonic type II neuroblast lineages contain more intermediate progenitors than Drosophila lineages.
source_text: These embryonic lineages are significantly larger in Tribolium than they are in Drosophila and contain more intermediate progenitors.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by quantitative data comparing the number of intermediate progenitors between species, as shown in Tables 1 and 2 and Figure 9.

claim: Tc-otd is absent from all type II neuroblasts and intermediate progenitors in Tribolium.
source_text: Notably, Tc-otd is absent from all type II neuroblasts and intermediate progenitors
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations using RNA in situ hybridization and antibody staining shown in Figure 10.

claim: Tc-six3 marks an anterior subset of type II neuroblast lineages in Tribolium.
source_text: whereas Tc-six3 marks an anterior subset of the type II lineages.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental data showing Tc-six3 expression in the four anterior-most lineages, as shown in Figure 11C.

claim: Tc-six4 specifically marks the territory where anterior-medial type II neuroblasts differentiate.
source_text: Tc-six4 specifically marks the territory where anterior-medial type II neuroblasts differentiate.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations of Tc-six4 expression patterns in relation to type II neuroblast positions, as shown in Figure 11A and B.

claim: Type II neuroblasts produce intermediate progenitors, which are cycling precursors that increase neural progeny.
source_text: These specific NBs generate more offspring by producing another class of neural precursors, the intermediate progenitors (INPs), which also divide in a stem cell-like fashion
evidence_reasoning: This claim draws from established scientific knowledge about type II neuroblasts, as referenced by citations to Walsh and Doe, 2017; Bayraktar and Doe, 2013.

claim: The central complex is produced in large parts by type II neuroblasts.
source_text: The central complex of the brain is an excellent model to understand neural development and divergence. It is produced in large parts by type II neuroblasts
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on established knowledge from prior research, as indicated by references to Boyan and Reichert, 2011; Boyan et al., 2017.

claim: Tribolium develops a functional larval central complex during embryogenesis.
source_text: with Tribolium developing a functional larval central complex during embryogenesis, whereas it develops only at the onset of adult life in Drosophila
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by references to previous work (Farnworth et al., 2020b; Koniszewski et al., 2016).

claim: Drosophila develops a functional central complex only at the onset of adult life.
source_text: with Tribolium developing a functional larval central complex during embryogenesis, whereas it develops only at the onset of adult life in Drosophila
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by references to previous research (Farnworth et al., 2020b; Koniszewski et al., 2016).

claim: Type II neuroblasts undergo repeated divisions producing intermediate progenitors.
source_text: They also undergo repeated divisions, with each round producing an intermediate progenitor cell (INP), which is also a proliferating progenitor
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on established knowledge about type II neuroblast behavior, as referenced in the manuscript (Bayraktar and Doe, 2013).

claim: Type I neuroblasts undergo stem cell-like divisions producing ganglion mother cells.
source_text: Type I NBs undergo stem cell-like divisions, with each round producing a ganglion mother cell (GMC) that divides one more time to produce two neurons or glia cells.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on established knowledge about type I neuroblast behavior, as indicated by the figure caption and references.

claim: Medial Drosophila type II neuroblasts produce an average of 450 neurons.
source_text: Medial Drosophila type II NBs produce an average of 450 neurons, whereas type I NBs of the brain only generate 100–200 neurons each
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to previous research (Bello et al., 2008; Boyan and Williams, 2011; Izergina et al., 2009).

claim: Type I neuroblasts of the Drosophila brain generate 100-200 neurons each.
source_text: Medial Drosophila type II NBs produce an average of 450 neurons, whereas type I NBs of the brain only generate 100–200 neurons each
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to previous research (Bello et al., 2008; Boyan and Williams, 2011; Izergina et al., 2009).

claim: Type II neuroblasts and intermediate progenitors are believed to be conserved among insects based on observations in grasshopper.
source_text: Based on descriptions of large proliferative lineages in the grasshopper S. gregaria, a hemimetabolous insect distantly related to flies, it is widely believed that type II NBs and INPs are conserved within insects
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on inferences from observations in grasshopper, as cited from Boyan and Reichert, 2011; Boyan et al., 2010.

claim: A molecular characterization of type II neuroblast lineages has not been performed in insects other than Drosophila prior to this study.
source_text: However, a molecular characterization of such lineages that, on the one hand, will allow to test whether the cell type markers characterized in Drosophila are more widely conserved, and, on the other hand, will facilitate an identification of subcell types, has not been performed in an insect other than Drosophila.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on a review of existing literature indicating the absence of such characterization in other insects.

claim: The fez-mm-eGFP enhancer trap line marks mushroom bodies in the larval brain of Tribolium.
source_text: We named the line fez magic mushrooms (fez-mm-eGFP) because it marks the mushroom bodies of the larval brain
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations of the enhancer trap line expression pattern shown in Figure 2.

claim: The fez-mm-eGFP reporter construct was inserted 160 bp upstream of the Tc-fez/erm transcription start site.
source_text: The reporter construct was inserted 160 bp upstream of the fez/erm-transcription start site using the non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) repair mechanism
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental methods and molecular characterization of the transgenic line.

claim: At embryonic stage NS11, seven Tc-pnt-clusters are present in a horse-shoe-shaped formation in Tribolium.
source_text: At stage NS11, seven Tc-pnt-clusters are present in a horse-shoe-shaped formation surrounding fez-mm-eGFP-positive cells
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations and imaging data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: At embryonic stage NS13, nine Tc-pnt-clusters are present in Tribolium, with seven in an anterior group and two in a posterior group.
source_text: At stage NS13, these groups are found in a position at the medial border of the head lobes and their number has increased to nine. The seven clusters that were already present at stage NS11 are arranged in an anterior group (white arrowheads in Figure 3B) at stage NS13 while two additional clusters have emerged more posteriorly
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations and imaging data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Type II neuroblasts in Tribolium have a significantly larger diameter (average 12.98 µm) than average cells of the embryonic head (average 6.75 µm).
source_text: We found that the cells that we had assigned as type II NBs had a significantly larger diameter (av.: 12.98 µm; n=43) than cells of the reference sample (av.: 6.75 µm; n=1579)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements and statistical analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: Nuclei of type II neuroblasts in Tribolium have a significantly larger diameter (average 8.73 µm) than nuclei of control cells (average 5.21 µm).
source_text: We also found that the diameters of nuclei of type II NBs were significantly larger (av.: 8.73 µm; n=17) than the ones of a control sample (av.: 5.21 µm; n=1080)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements and statistical analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: Tc-pnt-positive type II neuroblasts in Tribolium express Tc-dpn.
source_text: We found that the large Tc-pnt-positive but fez-mm-eGFP-negative cells (i.e., type II NBs) express the gene Tc-dpn
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations using HCR and antibody staining shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Type II neuroblasts in Tribolium do not express Tc-ase.
source_text: Like Drosophila type II NBs, these cells do not express the type I NB marker Tc-ase
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Immature Tc-pnt-positive intermediate progenitors in Tribolium do not express Tc-ase.
source_text: We further found additional cells directly adjacent of the type II NBs itself, which we believe are recently born immature INPs. They are Tc-pnt-positive but fez-mm-eGFP-negative and neither express Tc-ase
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Expression of Tc-ase starts in immature Tc-pnt-positive intermediate progenitors in Tribolium.
source_text: Expression of Tc-ase starts in the following in immature Tc-pnt-positive INPs
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations of gene expression patterns shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Tc-dpn is absent from immature Tc-pnt-positive intermediate progenitors but is expressed in mature intermediate progenitors in Tribolium.
source_text: Tc-dpn is absent from immature Tc-pnt-positive INPs (Figure 5D, pink arrowhead) but is expressed in mature INPs
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations shown in Figure 5B and 5D.

claim: Tc-pros is expressed in mature intermediate progenitors and ganglion mother cells in Tribolium.
source_text: We found the gene Tc-pros expressed in most fez-mm-eGFP expressing cells of a lineage (in Figure 6A and B) and infer from the extent of the expression that it is expressed in mature INPs (Tc-dpn+) and GMCs (Tc-dpn-)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations and logical inference from expression patterns shown in Figure 6.

claim: The expression dynamics of neural markers in Tribolium type II neuroblast lineages are very similar to those found in Drosophila.
source_text: In summary, the expression dynamics found in the Tribolium type II NB lineages are very similar to the one found in Drosophila
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on comparative analysis of gene expression patterns between the two species, supported by experimental data in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: Type II neuroblast lineages in Tribolium produce central complex cells marked by shaking hands (skh).
source_text: By co-staining for Tc-pnt and Tc-fez/erm RNA in the background of the skh-line, we found that the skh-positive cells are located directly distally of the type II NB lineages in a position where the type II NBs-derived neural cells are expected
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations using the skh reporter line shown in Figure 8.

claim: Both the anterior-median and posterior groups of type II neuroblasts contribute to central complex neuropile in Tribolium.
source_text: We found skh cells at the end of lineages of the anterior-median group (Figure 8A) and at the end the two posterior lineages (Figure 8B). We therefore conclude that both groups contribute to central complex neuropile
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on experimental observations of skh expression and logical inference about lineage contributions shown in Figure 8.

claim: At stage NS13, each Tribolium type II neuroblast lineage consisted on average of 18.4 progenitor cells.
source_text: We found that at stage NS13 (early retracting embryo) each lineage consisted on average of 18.4 progenitor cells
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by quantitative cell counting data presented in Table 1.

claim: At stage NS14, each Tribolium type II neuroblast lineage consisted on average of 16.8 progenitor cells.
source_text: and at stage NS14 (retracted embryo) of 16.8 progenitors
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by quantitative cell counting data presented in Table 1.

claim: Between 5 and 10% of cells in Tribolium type II neuroblast lineages were marked by the PH3 antibody indicating mitotic activity.
source_text: Between 5 and 10% of the cells were marked by the PH3 antibody.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by quantitative analysis of PH3 staining data.

claim: Beetle type II neuroblast lineages are significantly larger than corresponding ones in Drosophila at comparable embryonic stages.
source_text: We found that the beetle lineages were significantly larger than the corresponding ones in Drosophila
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by comparative quantitative analysis shown in Figure 9 and statistical testing.

claim: Embryonic type II neuroblast lineages in Tribolium comprise significantly more mature intermediate progenitors than corresponding lineages in Drosophila.
source_text: We also found that the embryonic type II NB lineages in Tribolium comprised significantly more mature INPs (Tc-dpn+/ Tc-fez+) than the corresponding lineages in Drosophila
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by comparative quantitative analysis shown in Figure 9 and statistical testing.

claim: Tc-otd is not expressed in type II neuroblasts or intermediate progenitors of both anterior-medial and posterior lineages in Tribolium.
source_text: We found no co-expression of fez-mm-eGFP marked cells of both the anterior-medial and posterior lineages with Tc-otd. Rather, Tc-otd was expressed in the surrounding embryonic head tissue. Tc-otd was also absent from the type II NBs themselves
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations using RNA in situ hybridization shown in Figure 10.

claim: Tc-six4 is expressed in the area where type II neuroblast clusters 1-6 of the anterior-medial group first differentiate in Tribolium.
source_text: Interestingly, we found that Tc-six4 is expressed specifically in that area of the head lobe in which the type II NBs clusters 1–6 of the anterior-medial group first differentiate.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations of Tc-six4 expression patterns shown in Figure 11A.

claim: At stage NS13, Tc-six4 marks both type II neuroblasts and fez-mm-eGFP-expressing intermediate progenitors in Tribolium.
source_text: At stage NS13, Tc-six4 marks both, type II NBs and fez-mm-eGFP-expressing INPs and some surrounding cells
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations shown in Figure 11A.

claim: At stage NS14, Tc-six4 marks type II neuroblasts of the anterior-medial group but is not expressed in fez-mm-eGFP intermediate progenitors in Tribolium.
source_text: At the following differentiation stage (NS14), Tc-six4 still marks the type II NBs clusters of the anterior-medial group but is not expressed in the fez-mm-eGFP INPs
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations shown in Figure 11B.

claim: Tc-six4 is not expressed in the posterior group of type II neuroblasts in Tribolium.
source_text: It is also not expressed in the posterior group of type II NBs but only marks type II NBs of the anterior-medial group.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations shown in Figure 11.

claim: Tc-six3 marks the anterior-most lineages 1-4 in Tribolium, including both type II neuroblasts and fez-mm-eGFP marked intermediate progenitors/ganglion mother cells.
source_text: Finally, we found that Tc-six3 marks, and is restricted to, the anterior-most lineages 1–4, including both the type II NBs and the fez-mm-eGFP marked INPs/GMCs
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations shown in Figure 11C.

claim: The higher number and greater lineage size of embryonic type II neuroblasts in beetle correlate with a previously described embryonic phase of central complex formation.
source_text: The higher number and greater lineage size of the embryonic type II neuroblasts in the beetle correlate with a previously described embryonic phase of central complex formation.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on the current experimental findings combined with inference and reference to previous work on central complex development timing.

claim: The insect central complex is an anterior, midline spanning neuropile that constitutes an important brain center for processing sensory input, coordination of movement, and navigation.
source_text: The insect central complex is an anterior, midline spanning neuropile and constitutes an important brain center for the processing of sensory input, coordination of movement, and navigation
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on established scientific knowledge about the central complex, as referenced by citations (Honkanen et al., 2019; Pfeiffer and Homberg, 2014).

claim: The basic structure of the central complex is highly conserved among different insect species.
source_text: The highly conserved basic structure of the central complex, along with diverse specifications in response to ecological requirements among different insect species, makes this brain structure a very interesting model for evolutionary developmental studies
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on established knowledge from comparative studies, as referenced by citations (Farnworth et al., 2020b; Koniszewski et al., 2016; Honkanen et al., 2019).

claim: Tribolium castaneum has emerged as a model for brain development and evolution.
source_text: Tribolium castaneum has emerged as a model for brain development and evolution.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on the established use of Tribolium in research, as supported by multiple citations in the manuscript.

claim: Many molecular genetic manipulation and labeling methods have been established in Tribolium.
source_text: In this beetle, many molecular genetic manipulation and labeling methods have been established
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by references to previous methodological work (Gilles et al., 2015; Gilles et al., 2019; Posnien et al., 2009; Farnworth et al., 2020a; Hunnekuhl et al., 2020).

claim: CRISPR-Cas9 has facilitated labeling of neural cell types in Tribolium.
source_text: Specifically, labeling of neural cell types in Tribolium has been facilitated by the advent of CRISPR-Cas9
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by references to previous work using CRISPR-Cas9 in Tribolium (Gilles et al., 2015; Farnworth et al., 2020a; He et al., 2019).

claim: Tribolium has more conserved development of the head neuroectoderm compared to Drosophila, facilitating identification of specific neurogenic domains.
source_text: Another factor that makes Tribolium an informative model for the understanding of insect brain development is the more conserved development of the head neuroectoderm facilitating the identification of specific neurogenic domains and allowing cross-species comparisons
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by references to previous comparative developmental studies (Posnien et al., 2023; Posnien et al., 2010; Posnien et al., 2011b).

claim: The entire insect central nervous system including the brain is produced by neural stem cells called neuroblasts.
source_text: The entire insect central nervous system including the brain is produced by neural stem cells, the neuroblasts (NBs)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on established knowledge about insect neurogenesis, as referenced by citation (Hartenstein and Stollewerk, 2015).

claim: Neuroblasts undergo repeated divisions producing rows of ganglion mother cells, which divide one more time to produce neurons and/or glia.
source_text: NBs undergo repeated divisions producing rows of ganglion mother cells (GMCs), which divide one more time to produce neurons and/or glia
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on established knowledge about neuroblast behavior, as referenced by citations (Doe and Skeath, 1996; Stollewerk, 2016).

claim: Type II neuroblasts were found to prominently contribute to the formation of the central complex in Drosophila and grasshopper.
source_text: Intriguingly, in Drosophila and in the grasshopper Schistocerca gregaria, an NB subtype, the type II NBs, were found to prominently contribute to the formation of the central complex
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by references to previous research (Boyan and Reichert, 2011; Boyan et al., 2017).

claim: Intermediate cycling progenitors have been described in vertebrates as radial glia cells.
source_text: Type II NBs and INPs have attracted a lot of attention because intermediate, cycling progenitors have also been described in vertebrates, the radial glia cells, which produce a variety of cell types
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by references to vertebrate neurobiology research (Malatesta et al., 2008; Barry et al., 2014).

claim: Brain tumors have been induced from type II neuroblast lineages in Drosophila.
source_text: In addition, in Drosophila, brain tumors have been induced from type II NB lineages
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by reference to previous research (Caussinus and Gonzalez, 2005).

claim: The characterization of type II neuroblasts in Drosophila has been based in large parts on an earmuff (fez/erm) enhancer element driving eGFP expression that marks intermediate progenitor lineages.
source_text: The characterization of type II NBs in Drosophila has in large parts been based on a specific reporter line in which eGFP expression is driven by an earmuff (fez/erm) enhancer element and marks INP lineages
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by references to previous work using this reporter line (Bayraktar and Doe, 2013; Pfeiffer et al., 2008; Weng et al., 2010).

claim: The ETS-transcription factor pointed (pnt) marks type II neuroblasts in Drosophila.
source_text: The ETS-transcription factor pointed (pnt) marks type II NBs
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by references to previous research (Xie et al., 2016; Zhu et al., 2011).

claim: Drosophila type II neuroblasts express deadpan (dpn) but not asense (ase).
source_text: which do not express the type I NB marker asense (ase) but the neural gene deadpan (dpn)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on established knowledge about Drosophila type II neuroblast markers, as indicated in Figure 1 and associated references.

claim: Intermediate progenitors in Drosophila express fez/erm and ase, and at a more mature stage also dpn.
source_text: INPs express fez/erm and ase and at a more mature stage also dpn
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on established knowledge about Drosophila intermediate progenitor markers, as referenced (Bayraktar and Doe, 2013; Bayraktar et al., 2010).

claim: Prospero (pros) marks mature intermediate progenitors and ganglion mother cells in Drosophila.
source_text: whereas prospero (pros) marks mature INPs and GMCs
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on established knowledge about Drosophila markers, as referenced (Bayraktar and Doe, 2013; Bayraktar et al., 2010).

claim: Six4 is a marker for Drosophila type II neuroblasts and intermediate progenitors.
source_text: Six4 is another marker for Drosophila type II NBs and INPs
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by reference to previous research (Chen et al., 2021).

claim: The fez-mm-eGFP line co-localized with most Tc-fez/erm-expressing cells in an area that gives rise to protocerebral structures including mushroom bodies, larval eyes, and central complex.
source_text: We found that at the embryonic stage fez-mm-eGFP co-localized with most Tc-fez/erm-expressing cells in an area that will give rise to the protocerebral structures mushroom bodies, larval eyes, and central complex
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations combined with references to previous work on these brain structures (Posnien et al., 2023; Posnien et al., 2011b).

claim: Large Tc-pnt-expressing cells and fez-mm-eGFP-expressing cells are mitotically active in Tribolium.
source_text: We also found that the large Tc-pnt-expressing cells as well as fez-mm-eGFP-expressing cells are mitotically active
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations using mitosis markers shown in Figure 3.

claim: The number of type II neuroblasts is not fixed across insects.
source_text: Our finding of an additional type II NB lineage at the embryonic stage shows that the number of type II NBs is not fixed across insects
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on the experimental finding of nine type II neuroblasts in Tribolium compared to eight in other insects, combined with logical inference.

claim: Evolutionary divergence in brain development between species may be driven by differences in the number of progenitor lineages.
source_text: Our finding of an additional type II NB lineage at the embryonic stage shows that the number of type II NBs is not fixed across insects and suggests that evolutionary divergence in brain development between species may be driven by differences in the number of progenitor lineages.
evidence_reasoning: This claim involves speculative reasoning based on the observed differences in type II neuroblast numbers between species.

claim: In Schistocerca, there is no obvious clustering of type II neuroblasts, and they are all arranged in one row at the medial rim of the head lobes.
source_text: In the hemimetabolan Schistocerca, there is no obvious clustering of type II NBs, and they are all arranged in one row at the medial rim of the head lobes.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on previous observations in grasshopper, though specific citations are not provided in this sentence.

claim: In Tribolium, type II neuroblasts are arranged into two groups per side: one large anterior-medial group containing seven type II neuroblast clusters and one posterior group of two type II neuroblasts.
source_text: In Tribolium, we have observed an arrangement of the type II NBs into two groups per side, one large anterior-medial group containing seven type II NB clusters and one posterior group of two type II NBs.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations and spatial mapping shown in Figure 3.

claim: In Drosophila, there are three groups of type II neuroblasts referred to as the anterior, middle, and posterior clusters.
source_text: In Drosophila, there are three described groups referred to as the anterior, the middle, and the posterior clusters
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by reference to previous research (Walsh and Doe, 2017).

claim: The Drosophila posterior cluster of type II neuroblasts consists of two type II neuroblasts and likely corresponds to the posterior two type II neuroblasts in Tribolium.
source_text: The posterior cluster consists of two type II NBs and therefore most likely corresponds to the posterior two type II NBs in Tribolium.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on logical inference from the comparison of type II neuroblast arrangements between species.

claim: There is a tendency toward grouping of type II neuroblasts into subsets in holometabolan models that was not observed in the only hemimetabolan studied so far.
source_text: In summary, there is a tendency toward grouping of type II NBs into subsets in the holometabolan models that was not observed in the only hemimetabolan studied so far.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on comparative analysis and inference from observations across different insect species.

claim: A ninth type II neuroblast was only found in the Tribolium embryo, representing a striking developmentally divergent feature.
source_text: A ninth type II NB was only found in the Tribolium embryo that represents a striking developmentally divergent feature
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on experimental observations combined with comparative inference.

claim: Expression of Tc-pnt and Tc-fez/erm in Tribolium is not completely mutually exclusive, with a small window of overlap in immature-II intermediate progenitors.
source_text: Despite both factors characterizing different stages of INP maturation, they are not completely mutually exclusive and we observed a small window of overlap in immature-II INPs
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental observations of gene expression patterns.

claim: The overlap of Tc-pnt and Tc-fez/erm expression is highly suggestive of a conserved role of Pnt in the activation of fez/erm.
source_text: Despite both factors characterizing different stages of INP maturation, they are not completely mutually exclusive and we observed a small window of overlap in immature-II INPs, highly suggestive of a conserved role of Pnt in the activation of fez/erm
evidence_reasoning: This claim combines experimental observations with inference and reference to previous work (Xie et al., 2016).

claim: Drosophila dpn is a neural marker expressed in type II neuroblasts and again in mature intermediate progenitors, leaving a gap of expression in immature-I and II intermediate progenitors.
source_text: Drosophila dpn is a neural marker (Bier et al., 1992) expressed in type II NBs and again in mature INPs, leaving a gap of expression in immature-I and II INPs.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on established knowledge from previous research (Bier et al., 1992).

claim: Drosophila ase is repressed in type II neuroblasts but expressed together with fez/erm in intermediate progenitors and ganglion mother cells where its expression overlaps with pros.
source_text: Drosophila ase is repressed in type II NBs but expressed together with fez/erm in INPs and GMCs where its expression overlaps with pros
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on established knowledge from previous research (Li et al., 2016).

claim: The expression dynamics of genes in Tribolium type II neuroblast lineages are identical to those found in Drosophila.
source_text: We found identical dynamics of gene expression in Tribolium
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on comparative analysis of gene expression patterns between the two species.

claim: The conserved expression dynamics suggest conservation of gene function within type II neuroblast lineages and a conserved process of intermediate progenitor maturation.
source_text: suggesting conservation of gene function within the lineages and a conserved process of INP maturation.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on logical inference from the observed conservation of gene expression patterns.

claim: Expression of genes examined in type II neuroblasts and their lineages is highly conserved between fly and beetle, which is implicit of conserved gene function and a conserved process of central complex formation.
source_text: In conclusion, expression of the genes examined in this study in type II NBs and their lineages is highly conserved in fly and beetle, which is implicit of conserved gene function and a conserved process of central complex formation.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on experimental observations combined with logical inference about functional conservation.

claim: Previous work described a heterochronic shift in central complex formation between fly and beetle.
source_text: Previous work described a heterochronic shift in central complex formation between fly and beetle
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by references to previous research (Farnworth et al., 2020b; Koniszewski et al., 2016).

claim: In Tribolium, parts of the central complex develop during embryogenesis and become functional at the onset of the first larval stage.
source_text: In Tribolium, parts of the central complex develop during embryogenesis. It becomes functional at the onset of the first larval stage
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by reference to previous research (Farnworth et al., 2020b).

claim: The functional central complex in Tribolium is presumably required for the more complex movements of beetle larvae using legs.
source_text: It becomes functional at the onset of the first larval stage and is presumably required for the more complex movements of the beetle larvae using legs
evidence_reasoning: This claim combines reference to previous work with speculative reasoning about functional requirements (Farnworth et al., 2020b).

claim: In both Drosophila and Tribolium, the anterior groups of type II neuroblasts are fully present in the last third of embryogenesis, with the beginning of germ band retraction.
source_text: In both Drosophila and Tribolium, the anterior groups of type II NBs (anterior-medial group of Tribolium and anterior and middle cluster of Drosophila) are fully present in the last third of embryogenesis, with the beginning of germ band retraction
evidence_reasoning: This claim combines experimental observations with references to previous work (Biffar and Stollewerk, 2014; Walsh and Doe, 2017; Campos-Ortega and Hartenstein, 1985).

claim: In the Drosophila embryo, only a limited number of intermediate progenitors and ganglion mother cells are produced before type II neuroblasts enter a resting stage prior to hatching.
source_text: However, in the Drosophila embryo, only a limited number of INPs and GMCs are produced before they enter a resting stage prior to hatching
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by reference to previous research (Walsh and Doe, 2017).

claim: The increased activity of type II neuroblast lineages in Tribolium may contribute to the embryonic development of a functional central body and protocerebral bridge.
